title: cocoon-agent-sandbox configuration, version 1
description: One file on the host, ~/.config/cocoon/sandbox.json, placed and edited by hand; never a repository's. Nothing is read from the environment; unknown keys are refused; an empty profile is the strictest container.

ref.description: the tag or branch the launcher downloads and runs; pin a tag

install.description: put the launcher on the PATH as `cocoon` when run from elsewhere (a fresh download); the installed copy never rewrites itself

bin.description: the directory to install into; absent: Linux ~/.local/bin; macOS Homebrew's prefix for the architecture when writable, else refused

image.description: the podman image name built from sandbox/

account.description: the GitHub account the agents' Apps are installed on

repo.description: owner/repo cloned into the workspace volume on first start

clones.description: owner/repo cloned beside the workspace on first start, ephemeral

profiles.description: named hosts lists (sandbox/configs/<name>.hosts) the host user may turn on for one session with `-- --<name>`

gateway.description: present: the wall allows the gateway's address alone and every tool reaches GitHub, npm and the research hosts through its subdomains; no App token is minted and none enters the container

domain.description: the parent of the gateway's subdomains, e.g. gw.example.com

address.description: the gateway's IPv4 address: the one host in the wall; the subdomains resolve to it inside the container (the example carries 203.0.113.10, a documentation address; the real one lives in the sandbox configuration on the box only)

upstreams.description: the subdomain names, the keys of the gateway's config/upstreams.json (github, git, npm, anthropic, arxiv, export-arxiv)

ca.description: host path of the private root's public half (root.crt from certs.sh); the container trusts it and nothing else for the gateway

model.description: route the agent's model API through the gateway's anthropic subdomain (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL); the agent's login hosts (<agent>-login.hosts) stay allowed directly in every shape, since the login's token refresh does not follow that variable

app_id.description: the GitHub App that is this agent's identity

key.description: host path of the App's private key, mode 600; never mounted

bot_id.description: the bot user's numeric id, for the no-reply email

config_volume.description: <volume>:<path in the container> for the agent's own state

tokens_file.description: host path of a mode-600 file with one KEY=value line the agent needs (read, never sourced)

env.description: environment set in the container for this agent, each line a reviewed decision

gateway.description: this agent's client identity at the gateway (certs.sh client <dir> <role>): required when the top-level gateway is present, refused otherwise

cert.description: host path of <role>.crt; the common name is the role

key.description: host path of <role>.key, mode 600; mounted read-only, read by the relay only

token.description: host path of <role>.token, mode 600, one line: the role's bearer token the relay adds as Proxy-Authorization
